questions.q: How does impact analysis differ from the lineage view covered in the previous lesson?
options: Lineage view maps how items connect; impact analysis quantifies which downstream items a planned change would affect, including items in other workspaces lineage view doesn't show
They are the exact same feature under two different names
Impact analysis only works on reports, while lineage view only works on lakehouses
Lineage view requires write permission, but impact analysis works for anyone with any access level
questions.explain: Lineage view shows structure within one workspace; impact analysis specifically sizes up the downstream blast radius of a change, reaching items and workspaces lineage view's one-workspace graph can't show.

questions.q: Where can you open impact analysis for an item?
options: From that item's card in lineage view, or from the Lineage dropdown on the item's own details page
Only from the Fabric tenant admin portal
Only from Power BI Desktop, never from the Fabric service
From the OneLake catalog's domain selector only
questions.explain: Both the impact analysis icon on a lineage-view card and the "Impact analysis" option in an item details page's Lineage dropdown open the same pane, scoped to that item.

questions.q: In the impact analysis pane, what's the difference between the "Child Items" and "All downstream items" tabs?
options: Child Items shows only the direct, one-step dependents; All downstream items shows every affected item further down the chain, including items in other workspaces
Child Items shows upstream sources, while All downstream items shows reports exclusively
The two tabs always return identical counts
All downstream items is visible only to tenant administrators
questions.explain: Child Items is a one-step view of direct dependents; All downstream items expands to the full chain, however many hops away, across workspaces.

questions.q: For a data source (rather than a dataset or report), how far can impact analysis show its downstream dependents?
options: Only its direct child items — to see further downstream, run impact analysis again on those direct children
Every downstream item across the entire tenant, several hops deep
Nothing; data sources are excluded from impact analysis entirely
Only items created in the same calendar month as the data source
questions.explain: Data sources are a documented limitation: impact analysis only shows their direct children, not the full downstream chain available for other item types.

questions.q: What permission do you need to run impact analysis on an item, and what happens to an affected item's name when you don't have access to it?
options: You need write permission on the item; items you can't access are shown as "Limited access" instead of their real name
No permission is required, and every item's real name is always shown
You need tenant admin rights, and inaccessible items are simply left out of the count entirely
Read-only Viewer access is enough, and restricted items show a blank row with no label
questions.explain: Write permission on the item is required to run impact analysis on it; for privacy, downstream items you lack access to are labeled "Limited access" rather than named, since a name itself can carry sensitive information.
